summary:
Senate Hearings on Energy
This past week, the U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation along with the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources held a joint and public hearing on energy pricing and profits. Each committee has 22 members for a total of 44 senators drawn together to cross examine five top executives from ExxonMobil, Chevron, ConocoPhillips, BP America, and Shell Oil.

children.title: U.S. Gasoline Consumption & Retail Price
children.summary: $/Gallon Gasoline Consumption For those who live and work in such places as Houston, Los Angeles, New York, Fairfax, you have probably not noticed a significant reduction in commuting times. The incremental cost of gasoline has gone up by about $20 per week (30 miles each way to work at 15 miles to the gallon for a SUV; a $1 dollar increase in gasoline prices translates to $4 per day round trip in extra commuting expenses.) This incremental $80 per month is nominal when compared to the increased mortgage payments that have resulted from rising interest rates caused by the looming deficits by the federal government and increased taxes thanks to the Alternative Minimum Tax.
